facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that leverage is better than it looks is that fiscal 2025 EBITDA was depressed by USD 86.3 million of ERP charges: on a normalised basis fiscal 2025 total debt over EBITDA would have been 4.04x and net debt 2.97x, so underlying leverage was already improving before 2026. The strongest case that it is worse is that reported EBITDA still carries environmental and restructuring costs, that cover and interest cost lean on swap receipts, and that the swaps mature in 2028 and 2029 and have been rolled rather than settled. The view would weaken if rolling EBITDA slipped back toward the fiscal 2025 level of USD 389.4 million, if the Calvert City accrual rose again, or if the swaps were settled in cash; it would strengthen if the 2029 term loan were refinanced well ahead of maturity and interim cash interest were disclosed. - Cash interest paid is not printed in any quarterly report, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30, and interim cover can only be shown on net interest expense as a proxy. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain interest paid for the interim periods or keep cover to fiscal years. Severity: Low. Action: use the annual figures with their period label. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain any management bridge, otherwise keep house adjustments labelled as Analyst Judgement. facts.text: Financial policy shown by actions is creditor-aligned. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a Low-risk reading is behavioural uncertainty, not a documented adverse act. Both senior officers named in the 2026 filings differ from the annual report with no explanation, a buyback authorisation equal to 5.40% of shares outstanding remains open and share repurchases are listed among the expected uses of cash for the rest of 2026, dividends exceeded fiscal 2025 earnings, and the unreserved tax claims and the open-ended Calvert City accrual could absorb the cash that now goes to term-loan prepayment. The view would worsen to Medium if new management announced debt-funded repurchases or an acquisition, if the proxy statement showed a large holder pressing for change, or if the executed debt documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity. It would firm up if the proxy statement showed dispersed holdings and an independent board, if the leadership changes were explained as planned succession, and if prepayments continued. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving profile is how recently it was weaker. Total debt was 4.94x EBITDA and net debt 3.63x at the end of 2025, operating income fell 38.2% in that year on flat sales, and the 2026 recovery rests partly on pricing that is not yet tested by a downturn, while 99.95% of principal comes due within three years of 2029. The strongest evidence for a better view is that net debt is falling, liquidity covers the 2029 maturity 1.98x and free cash flow of USD 239.0 million is 45.84% of EBITDA. The view would weaken if the last-twelve-months EBITDA margin fell below the 14.59% of normalised fiscal 2025, if the Calvert City accrual rose again, if the swaps were settled in cash, or if new management announced debt-funded buybacks or an acquisition. It would strengthen if the 2029 term loan were refinanced well before maturity, if cash interest were disclosed for interim periods, or if the debt documents showed covenant headroom and priority terms. facts.label: Business model and revenue durability
facts.text: Avient formulates specialty polymer materials from purchased resins and additives and sells them through two segments, Color, Additives and Inks and Specialty Engineered Materials, which together produced sales of USD 3,260.2 million in fiscal 2025. Revenue is order-driven with short manufacturing lead times, contract tenor and renewal rates are not supplied, and no customer exceeded 3% of revenue, so visibility comes from breadth rather than from a stated backlog, with defense tenders the main lumpy exception. Fiscal 2025 sales were flat and growth returned in 2026, with third-quarter sales up 10.5% on packaging, building and construction, industrial, consumer and energy demand and pricing actions, and nine-month sales up 6.2% of which 4.2% was organic. For creditors this means cash flow is steady but follows industrial and consumer demand and input prices, so debt service capacity depends on keeping price ahead of cost. facts.label: Cost structure, margins and cash conversion
facts.text: Cost of sales was 68.85% of fiscal 2025 sales and selling and administrative expense 24.91%, so most cost is variable with resin, pigment and energy prices, which the company warns may not move with selling prices. That gives some flexibility to cut cost with volume but leaves margin exposed to a price lag, and the operating margin of 6.24% in fiscal 2025 against 10.16% in fiscal 2024 shows how charges and cost swings move it. Capital spending of 3.18% of last-twelve-months sales and the cost savings the company cites from productivity and restructuring actions support conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow, 50.08% in fiscal 2025 and 45.84% over the last twelve months, while working capital absorbed USD 138.8 million in nine months of 2026 against USD 135.3 million a year earlier, a normal seasonal build. Cash interest, cash taxes and restructuring cash all sit below EBITDA, so the conversion is a better guide to debt service capacity than the EBITDA ratios. facts.label: Ownership and financial policy
facts.text: Avient is a public company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in the filings, and its consolidated perimeter is the only group structure supplied; borrower and guarantor perimeters and the priority of the notes against the secured term loan and revolver are not established. Financial policy shown by action is conservative: debt was prepaid from cash, no shares were repurchased, the dividend rose each year and no acquisition has been paid for since 2022, so leverage tolerance appears to have fallen as net leverage moved from 3.63x to 2.65x. The unexplained change of chief executive and chief financial officer in 2026, and a buyback authorisation that remains open, are the points that could change that policy. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F01; calculation F02

facts.label: Industry forces and credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Competition is global and local: the company competes with global companies and local niche producers on performance, innovation, service, quality, delivery and price, and with polymer and non-polymer alternatives, so rivalry limits price increases beyond cost pass-through. Buyer power is dispersed because no customer exceeds 3% of revenue, while supplier power sits with large chemical producers, whose resin and additive prices Avient cannot control and, for some strategic materials, cannot easily replace. Trade policy and currency are the material external factors: the annual report names tariffs and retaliatory measures as risks to demand and results, 61% of sales are outside the United States, and the euro net investment is hedged with swaps whose liability is USD 302.0 million, so a stronger dollar or new tariffs would pressure translated earnings, while plastics and environmental regulation add compliance cost. In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, cash generation and diversification, the weaknesses are the maturity wall, legacy claims and swap-supported interest cost, the opportunities are growth in defense, healthcare, electronics and infrastructure applications where growth-vector sales are outpacing the rest of the company, and the threats are input-cost inflation without pricing, tariffs and a weaker refinancing market in 2029 to 2031. facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the supports are pricing and mix, growth in defense, packaging and infrastructure demand, restructuring savings and lower interest from prepayments, while the pressures are input-cost inflation, tariffs, the Calvert City cost and timeline, tax claims and a fourth-quarter capital spending step-up toward the 2026 estimate of about USD 140 million. No guidance or forecast is supplied, so the outlook is qualitative: leverage should keep falling if the margin holds, but each of the pressures draws on cash that now goes to prepayment. Over three to five years the outlook is dominated by refinancing the term loan in 2029, the notes and revolver in 2030 and the 2031 notes, with swap maturities between 2027 and 2029 adding a possible cash call. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside starts with raw-material, energy and freight costs rising faster than selling prices in packaging, consumer and industrial markets, which the annual report names as a risk. The first operational break is gross margin, because cost of sales is most of the cost base and pass-through has only been shown in an upswing. If EBITDA fell back to its fiscal 2025 reported level, a fall of USD 132.0 million, total debt would be 4.69x EBITDA and net debt 3.55x, and free cash flow after dividends would be about USD 6.6 million before tax relief and working-capital release, so debt reduction would stop and the prepayment would have to come from cash. Management levers are the dividend of USD 100.4 million a year, capital spending that runs at about 57% of depreciation and amortization, restructuring and the unused buyback authority, and liquidity of USD 932.4 million would absorb the shortfall, so liquidity distress before 2029 is not indicated. The consequence is on refinancing: the USD 470.7 million term loan due in 2029 becomes current in 2028 and would be refinanced at 3.55x to 4.69x leverage and with Calvert City costs still open. The observable triggers are a falling EBITDA margin, a lag between price and cost, a rising environmental accrual and a swap settlement. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Avient presents an adequate business profile supported by diversified customers, steady free cash flow and USD 932.4 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by a USD 1,847.6 million maturity wall from 2029 to 2031 and by legacy claims that are not bounded. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow of USD 239.0 million covers dividends of USD 100.4 million and low capital spending, although part of the 2026 earnings gain is charges leaving the window. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and 2029, the margin holding, the Calvert City accrual stabilising and the treatment of the swap liabilities. The primary downside path is a pricing squeeze that returns EBITDA toward its 2025 level and leaves less cushion for refinancing. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant levels, the swap schedule, interim cash interest, a peer set and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: refinancing of the 2029 to 2031 maturity wall. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation F06; calculation F07; calculation F08; calculation F19

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five periodic filings support a snapshot of Avient's consolidated credit profile to 30 September 2026, but not covenant, security, guarantor, rating or market-price conclusions, which stay not established for lack of debt agreements and market inputs. For creditors this means leverage, liquidity and maturities can be analysed from audited and interim statements, while lien priority and covenant headroom cannot.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 89–91

The latest filing was signed 14 days before the as-of date and nothing later is supplied. Liquidity of USD 932.4 million at 30 September 2026 foots to cash and revolver availability, and the debt table foots to the balance sheet, so the headline debt and liquidity figures are usable. Two items need care: the names of the chief executive and chief financial officer changed during 2026 without any filing in the set explaining it, and management now assumes the Calvert City environmental clean-up will finish in 2032, two years later than before.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-06

## Findings
### Bottom line

Avient's net leverage fell to 2.65x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, from 3.63x at the end of 2025, but the gain is earnings recovery rather than debt reduction, so creditors depend on earnings holding. Net debt fell only USD 31.1 million in nine months, while last-twelve-months EBITDA rose USD 132.0 million to USD 521.4 million, of which USD 86.3 million is 2025 ERP charges leaving the window.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C34; calculation C31; calculation C14; calculation C55; calculation C52

Liquidity of USD 932.4 million exceeds the USD 471.1 million falling due in 2029, but cash interest cover was only 3.99x in fiscal 2025 and leans on cross-currency swap receipts, and Calvert City environmental costs of USD 19.1 million in the quarter show an obligation that is still growing.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation C40
### Key findings

Reported leverage moved in two steps. Total debt over reported EBITDA was 5.39x in fiscal 2023, 4.06x in fiscal 2024 and 4.94x in fiscal 2025, when USD 86.3 million of ERP impairment and hosting charges depressed EBITDA, and 3.50x at 30 September 2026; net debt over EBITDA followed the same path at 3.98x, 2.99x, 3.63x and 2.65x. The 2026 gain is mostly earnings: EBITDA for nine months was USD 434.7 million against USD 302.7 million, and USD 45.7 million of the USD 132.0 million increase is underlying once the 2025 charges are set aside. Debt moved little: total debt fell USD 95.9 million through USD 100.0 million of voluntary term loan prepayments, but cash fell USD 64.8 million, so net debt fell only USD 31.1 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 54–56; calculation C50; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C53; calculation C54; calculation C55; calculation C66

Cash interest cover was 3.63x in fiscal 2023, 5.97x in fiscal 2024 and 3.99x in fiscal 2025, and no interim cash interest is printed, so cover for 2026 is not calculable. The measure uses interest paid net of hedging, and cross-currency swaps returned USD 36.1 million in fiscal 2025; adding that back to the USD 97.6 million of cash interest would put cover near 2.91x, an Analyst Judgement. On net interest expense, which also nets the swap receipts, last-twelve-months cover is 5.81x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C59; calculation C60; calculation C22; calculation C14

Cash conversion is steady and capital intensity low. Operating cash flow was USD 301.6 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 347.8 million over the last twelve months, which after capital expenditures converted 50.08% and 45.84% of EBITDA into free cash flow, with capital expenditures at 3.27% of sales in fiscal 2025. Receivables, inventories and payables absorbed USD 138.8 million in the first nine months of 2026, close to the USD 135.3 million of the prior-year period, so the seasonal build is normal; after USD 75.7 million of dividends, nine-month free cash flow left USD 37.9 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C43; calculation C46; calculation C20; calculation C48; calculation C49; calculation C47

Liquidity was USD 932.4 million at 30 September 2026, made of USD 445.7 million of cash and USD 486.7 million of revolver availability, against USD 1,000.8 million at the end of 2025; about 83% of the cash is outside the United States. Only USD 1.0 million of principal falls due before 2029, then USD 471.1 million in 2029, USD 725.5 million in 2030 and USD 651.0 million thereafter, so USD 1,847.6 million of principal sits in a three-year window from 2029 to 2031, and the undrawn revolver matures in June 2030 alongside the 2030 notes.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C40; calculation C39; calculation C62; calculation C61

Several claims sit outside the USD 1,827.2 million of carrying-value debt. Cross-currency swap liabilities were USD 302.0 million at 30 September 2026, down from USD 380.9 million at the end of 2025, and the issuer has amended and extended the swaps rather than settling them in cash. Environmental accruals were USD 142.9 million, which the issuer says will probably be exceeded, with the Calvert City barrier wall now assumed complete in 2032. Operating lease obligations were USD 95.0 million undiscounted at the end of 2025, and the IRS 2019 matter claims USD 37.2 million of tax, interest and penalty with no provision, plus a 2022 matter with no amount printed. Pension plans were net overfunded by USD 4.7 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C63; calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C67

The figures rest on EBITDA that this analysis derives, because the issuer states none, and on carrying-value debt of USD 1,827.2 million against principal of USD 1,848.6 million. No supplier finance, factoring or customer-funded float was found, and no event after the balance-sheet date is stated; the one flagged subsequent event is the 2025 decision to stop ERP development, which the FY2024 annual report dated after its own balance sheet and which is kept out of fiscal 2024.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that leverage is better than it looks is that fiscal 2025 EBITDA was depressed by USD 86.3 million of ERP charges: on a normalised basis fiscal 2025 total debt over EBITDA would have been 4.04x and net debt 2.97x, so underlying leverage was already improving before 2026. The strongest case that it is worse is that reported EBITDA still carries environmental and restructuring costs, that cover and interest cost lean on swap receipts, and that the swaps mature in 2028 and 2029 and have been rolled rather than settled. The view would weaken if rolling EBITDA slipped back toward the fiscal 2025 level of USD 389.4 million, if the Calvert City accrual rose again, or if the swaps were settled in cash; it would strengthen if the 2029 term loan were refinanced well ahead of maturity and interim cash interest were disclosed.

## Gaps

- Cash interest paid is not printed in any quarterly report, so EBITDA over cash interest is not calculable for 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30, and interim cover can only be shown on net interest expense as a proxy. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain interest paid for the interim periods or keep cover to fiscal years.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Cash taxes paid are printed for fiscal years only, so interim cash taxes and free cash flow after tax for 2026 are not established. Severity: Low. Action: use the annual figures with their period label.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78

- The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, no add-backs and no management bridge, so the adjusted EBITDA row, the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied and reported EBITDA is derived by this analysis. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain any management bridge, otherwise keep house adjustments labelled as Analyst Judgement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Financial test levels and definitions are not printed and the credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable at any date. The filings say only that the revolver requires compliance with financial tests under certain circumstances and that the company complied with all covenants. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Ranking, guarantors and collateral are not stated for the revolver, the term loan, the 2030 notes or the other debt, and the FY2024 annual report calls only the 2031 notes senior unsecured obligations, so the debt stack is not drawn and debt by seniority is not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed agreements and indentures.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 89–91

- Letters-of-credit usage is not printed in the 2026 reports, so net availability rests on the issuer's printed availability of USD 486.7 million; the implied difference from the commitment is USD 13.3 million but is not stated as letters of credit. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the current letters-of-credit schedule.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Revolver availability at 2023-12-31 is not printed, so liquidity for fiscal 2023 is not established, and fiscal 2024 availability reflects the earlier revolver that was replaced in June 2025. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the current position.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 41

- The statements print a dash for Other income (expense), net in the third quarter of 2025 and for Proceeds from long-term borrowings in fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025; these are held as not supplied rather than zero. Severity: Low. Action: none.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56

- Payments on long-term borrowings and Proceeds from long-term borrowings are not printed in the first-quarter statements, and the interim reports print no proceeds line, so those cells are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none; the six- and nine-month statements carry the payments.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_avnt_avnt-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_avnt_avnt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The filings give maturities in aggregate only, so the term loan's scheduled amortisation, the exact maturity dates of the term loan and 2030 notes, the revolver margin and the composition of other debt are not stated; the notes are shown with no scheduled amortisation because the ladder shows only USD 1.0 million of principal due before 2029 across all debt. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the indentures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

- The swap maturity schedule after the June and July 2026 extensions is not printed, so which swaps make up the current liability of USD 97.2 million is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the current derivative schedule.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85

- The IRS draft notice of proposed adjustment on the 2022 capital loss, received in September 2026, has no amount and no reserve, so the size of that claim is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: monitor for the notice amount.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

- The Calvert City accrual is open-ended: the issuer says additional costs above the accrual are probable and cannot be estimated, and the barrier wall completion date moved to 2032 in the third quarter, so the total environmental claim is not bounded. Severity: High. Action: track each quarterly accrual and any record-of-decision change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Environmental cost is stated on two definitions in the third-quarter report, USD 19.1 million and USD 27.7 million in the contingencies note against USD 18.3 million and USD 26.6 million in the segment reconciliation, and the report does not reconcile them. Severity: Low. Action: quote each with its definition.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23
- The interim statements are unaudited and no auditor review is stated, so 2026 figures carry a lower evidence tier than fiscal years. Severity: Low. Action: none.

spans.text: # Avient Corp (avnt-1122976): Business, ownership and transaction facts, as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Issuer: Avient Corp (avnt-1122976), a listed Ohio company reporting on a consolidated basis; as-of date 2026-11-18; pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the business, ownership, transaction and operating-model facts, the governance and sponsor-behaviour read-through, and the issuer's dated history, as they bear on creditors, from the five supplied filings.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | Signed 2026-11-04 (filing date not stated) | 18c4bb686a8163d9e83cbe290ac66757579459c9a66885d10029469db6de24a4 | Latest period: segments, end-market drivers, debt, prepayments, swaps, legacy environmental and tax matters, share count, officer names. |
| Handoff module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | 7f8c226f27e5b07e6b1cea118fb50a9aaca47218445b979468c11169d275f0e2 | Source inventory, document dates, reporting perimeter and the gap ledger for the five filings; the gaps it names on debt documents, officer changes and the proxy statement are carried into this module's gap lines. |

No other handoff was supplied to this module. One correction to Source readiness: it records the filing date of the 2024 annual report as not stated, but the 2025 annual report says the earlier report was filed with the SEC on 2025-02-18, which this module uses.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Avient shows no sponsor, controlling holder or pending transaction in the filings supplied, so creditor risk lies in operations and legacy liabilities, and owner behaviour is not established as a driver. Sponsor and governance risk is Low on this evidence, with board control and covenant capacity unverified.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Source readiness (CP-0)

Actions so far favour creditors: USD 250.0 million of term loan was prepaid from cash in 2025 and 2026 and no shares were repurchased over the same period, while fiscal 2025 dividends paid took 50.67% of free cash flow and dividends declared equalled 121.25% of attributable net income. The unexplained change of both chief executive and chief financial officer in 2026 and the open-ended Calvert City clean-up are what could change that view.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C16
### Key findings

Ownership and control are not established beyond the absence of a named sponsor, which limits what can be said about owner behaviour. The filings name no sponsor, parent, controlling holder or special voting right, the common shares are listed in New York, and no shares were repurchased in 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026 although an authorisation equal to 5.40% of shares outstanding remains open. Holder concentration, board independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a large holder or an activist cannot be ruled out, and creditors face event risk from a change of control or a debt-funded return of capital that the supplied evidence neither shows nor excludes.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C23; Source readiness (CP-0)

Financial policy shown by actions is creditor-aligned. The company prepaid USD 150.0 million of the senior secured term loan in 2025 and USD 100.0 million in 2026 from cash on hand, without penalty, so total debt principal fell USD 100.3 million in nine months to USD 1,848.6 million and the senior secured term loan shrank to USD 470.7 million. It also replaced the 2025 notes with 2031 senior unsecured notes in 2024 and a new USD 500.0 million revolver running to 2030 in 2025, so refinancing has been done early and without new money. The mechanism is lower interest cost and a smaller secured claim ranking ahead of the unsecured notes on collateral value, although collateral and guarantor terms are not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C16; calculation C17

Dividends are the only recurring cash distribution to common shareholders; they are covered by cash flow but were not covered by fiscal 2025 earnings. Declared dividends of USD 99.3 million equal 121.25% of net income attributable to common shareholders, which carried USD 71.6 million of ERP impairment, yet dividends paid of USD 98.8 million took 50.67% of free cash flow of USD 195.0 million. In the first nine months of 2026 dividends of USD 75.7 million took 66.64% of free cash flow of USD 113.6 million, leaving USD 37.9 million, so the USD 100.0 million prepayment drew on cash. The dividend per share rose 4.25% in fiscal 2024 and 4.08% in fiscal 2025, a fixed cash call that is affordable on current cash flow but competes with debt reduction.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C19

The 2026 change of both the chief executive and the chief financial officer is the main governance uncertainty. The first-quarter report, signed on 2026-05-07, names Ashish K. Khandpur as Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer and Jamie A. Beggs as Chief Financial Officer; the second-quarter report names Giuseppe Di Salvo as Chief Financial Officer; and the third-quarter report names Michael J. Frank as President and Chief Executive Officer without a Chairman title. No supplied filing announces, dates or explains either change, or says who chairs the board, so continuity of dividend, buyback, acquisition and leverage policy is unproven and the Low risk level is conditional on that policy holding.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_avnt_avnt-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_avnt_avnt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_avnt_avnt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; Source readiness (CP-0)

The business is diversified by customer and region but exposed to input costs and to the pace of pricing. No customer exceeded 3% of 2025 consolidated revenue, and fiscal 2025 sales of USD 3,260.2 million split 62.39% Color, Additives and Inks and 37.77% Specialty Engineered Materials, with 40.16% from the United States and Canada, 36.06% from EMEA, 18.19% from Asia and 5.59% from Latin America. The 2026 recovery is partly price: nine-month sales rose 6.2% with organic growth of 4.2%, operating margins widened to 16.44% in Color, Additives and Inks and 14.91% in Specialty Engineered Materials from 15.48% and 13.31%, and management says pricing actions offset input inflation, while its own risk factor warns that raw-material and energy costs may not move with selling prices. If pass-through lags, the margin gain could reverse before debt is reduced.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07

Legacy claims outside debt are the main exposure that cannot be bounded, and they are growing rather than settling. The Calvert City accrual was USD 133.9 million at 2026-09-30 within total environmental accruals of USD 142.9 million, the filing says further costs above the accrual are probable and cannot be estimated, and charges were USD 56.8 million in 2023, USD 19.8 million in 2024, USD 21.3 million in 2025 and USD 27.7 million in the first nine months of 2026, with the completion assumption moving to 2032. The obligation traces to a 1993 indemnity given by Avient's predecessor, not to an owner decision, and USD 28.1 million of the USD 141.2 million obligation at the end of 2025 was due within a year, so the cash call competes with debt service; two unreserved IRS matters add a 2019 claim of USD 37.2 million and a second claim of unstated size.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C20; calculation C25; calculation C28

No transaction is pending and the last large moves were in 2022. The sale of the Distribution business for USD 950.0 million cash and business acquisitions of USD 1,426.1 million reshaped the group, and the cash flow statements show no payments for business acquisitions after 2022. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 3,129.5 million are 52.64% of total assets and exceed total equity by USD 658.8 million, so book equity rests on acquired intangibles and an impairment would hit equity rather than cash.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C18

The company has extended, not settled, its cross-currency swap liabilities. Swap liabilities were USD 302.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 380.9 million at the end of 2025, and in June and July 2026 swaps of EUR 700 million and EUR 200 million were moved out to June 2029 and August 2028 with the liability blended into the new contracts. This hedges the euro net investment and returns interest receipts, but a cash settlement would be a call on liquidity, and management's description of laddered maturities sits beside USD 1,847.6 million of principal, 99.95% of the total, falling due in the three years to 2031.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C21; calculation C26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Low-risk reading is behavioural uncertainty, not a documented adverse act. Both senior officers named in the 2026 filings differ from the annual report with no explanation, a buyback authorisation equal to 5.40% of shares outstanding remains open and share repurchases are listed among the expected uses of cash for the rest of 2026, dividends exceeded fiscal 2025 earnings, and the unreserved tax claims and the open-ended Calvert City accrual could absorb the cash that now goes to term-loan prepayment. The view would worsen to Medium if new management announced debt-funded repurchases or an acquisition, if the proxy statement showed a large holder pressing for change, or if the executed debt documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity. It would firm up if the proxy statement showed dispersed holdings and an independent board, if the leadership changes were explained as planned succession, and if prepayments continued.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C14; calculation C23
### Limitations

- Holder concentration and board independence are not established, so the conclusion that no one controls the issuer holds only as none named; a block holder could change creditor risk through a sale or an activist campaign.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88

- The executed credit agreement, term loan agreement and indentures are not supplied, so restricted-payment and debt capacity is not established and the finding that dividends are affordable rests on cash flow alone, not on covenant room.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68
- No filing after the third-quarter report is supplied, so any announcement that explains the 2026 officer changes, or any later transaction, is not established and could move the Low risk level.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

- Business descriptions and strategy statements are management's own words, and no independent market-share, end-market percentage or pricing-contract data is supplied, so the finding on revenue durability rests on the absence of a customer above 3% and on reported growth.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

- The 2022 acquisition is visible only through cash flow, hedging and restructuring notes because earlier annual reports are not supplied, so the finding that acquisitions are not a current pattern rests on the absence of acquisition payments after 2022.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2024-12-31_avnt_avnt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or new debt issue is stated for 2026 in the three quarterly reports, and nothing after the third-quarter report's signature on 2026-11-04 is supplied, so there is no pending transaction to underwrite and the position is as of that date. The cash flow statement for the first nine months of 2026 shows no borrowing proceeds, only dividends, term-loan repayments and other financing items.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

The recent financing record is liability management, not new money. The 2031 senior unsecured notes of USD 650.0 million were issued on 2024-09-19 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the 2025 notes in full; the senior secured term loan was repriced on 2024-04-09 and on 2025-03-12; a revolver of up to USD 500.0 million maturing 2030-06-12 replaced the 2026 facility on 2025-06-12; and the term loan was prepaid by USD 150.0 million in 2025 and USD 100.0 million in 2026 from cash on hand. spans.text: # Avient Corp (avnt-1122976): Fundamental credit view, as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Issuer: Avient Corp (avnt-1122976), a listed Ohio company reporting consolidated US GAAP statements in USD millions; as-of date 2026-11-18; pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the overall fundamental credit profile, its main support and constraints, the primary downside path and the signals to monitor, from the five supplied filings and the three earlier module outputs.
## Sources

The earlier modules are used as supplied; this module recomputes every ratio it quotes from printed figures and marks where it adds judgement.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Avient's credit profile is adequate and improving, supported by USD 932.4 million of liquidity and no material maturity before 2029, but a concentrated 2029 to 2031 wall and open-ended legacy costs make creditors dependent on earnings holding.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F08; calculation F19

Reported net leverage of 2.65x last-twelve-months EBITDA is down from 3.63x at the end of 2025, but only USD 45.7 million of the USD 132.0 million EBITDA gain is underlying, so the profile is Average, not Strong. The primary downside is a pricing squeeze that returns EBITDA toward its 2025 level while dividends of USD 100.4 million, restructuring and Calvert City cash calls continue.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F02; calculation F05; calculation F07; calculation F11
### Key findings

The business profile is Average: sizeable and diversified by customer and region, but without evidence of pricing power beyond the 2026 pass-through. Last-twelve-months sales were USD 3,416.2 million, no customer exceeded 3% of 2025 consolidated revenue and 61% of sales were outside the United States, which spreads demand risk across end markets and currencies. Gross margin fell to 31.2% in fiscal 2025 from 32.6% as costs and restructuring rose, and management says 2026 pricing actions offset input inflation, so pass-through has held so far but is untested in a downturn, and no peer set is supplied to benchmark it.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_avnt_avnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F03

Earnings are recovering, but about two thirds of the 2026 EBITDA gain is charges leaving the window, so the recovery is smaller than the leverage ratios suggest. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 521.4 million is USD 132.0 million above fiscal 2025, of which USD 86.3 million is the 2025 ERP impairment and hosting charges and USD 45.7 million, or 34.62%, is underlying. The margin of 15.26% compares with 14.64% for fiscal 2024 without a USD 34.7 million insurance gain and 14.59% for fiscal 2025 with the ERP charges added back, so the underlying margin rose by 0.62 percentage points to 0.67 percentage points over two years on mix and price. The issuer states no EBITDA, so these are derived figures, and environmental and restructuring costs remain inside them.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_avnt_avnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation F03; calculation F04; calculation F05

Cash generation is a support, but debt reduction is currently running ahead of it. Free cash flow was USD 239.0 million over the last twelve months, 45.84% of EBITDA, with capital expenditures at 56.96% of depreciation and amortization, and USD 138.6 million remained after dividends of USD 100.4 million. In the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow after dividends of USD 37.9 million funded only part of the USD 100.0 million term-loan prepayment and cash fell USD 64.8 million. Low capital intensity gives room to cut spending in a downturn, although the 2026 estimate of about USD 140 million implies a heavier fourth quarter.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving profile is how recently it was weaker. Total debt was 4.94x EBITDA and net debt 3.63x at the end of 2025, operating income fell 38.2% in that year on flat sales, and the 2026 recovery rests partly on pricing that is not yet tested by a downturn, while 99.95% of principal comes due within three years of 2029. The strongest evidence for a better view is that net debt is falling, liquidity covers the 2029 maturity 1.98x and free cash flow of USD 239.0 million is 45.84% of EBITDA. The view would weaken if the last-twelve-months EBITDA margin fell below the 14.59% of normalised fiscal 2025, if the Calvert City accrual rose again, if the swaps were settled in cash, or if new management announced debt-funded buybacks or an acquisition. ### Business model and revenue durability

Avient formulates specialty polymer materials from purchased resins and additives and sells them through two segments, Color, Additives and Inks and Specialty Engineered Materials, which together produced sales of USD 3,260.2 million in fiscal 2025. Revenue is order-driven with short manufacturing lead times, contract tenor and renewal rates are not supplied, and no customer exceeded 3% of revenue, so visibility comes from breadth rather than from a stated backlog, with defense tenders the main lumpy exception. Fiscal 2025 sales were flat and growth returned in 2026, with third-quarter sales up 10.5% on packaging, building and construction, industrial, consumer and energy demand and pricing actions, and nine-month sales up 6.2% of which 4.2% was organic. For creditors this means cash flow is steady but follows industrial and consumer demand and input prices, so debt service capacity depends on keeping price ahead of cost.

### Cost structure, margins and cash conversion

Cost of sales was 68.85% of fiscal 2025 sales and selling and administrative expense 24.91%, so most cost is variable with resin, pigment and energy prices, which the company warns may not move with selling prices. That gives some flexibility to cut cost with volume but leaves margin exposed to a price lag, and the operating margin of 6.24% in fiscal 2025 against 10.16% in fiscal 2024 shows how charges and cost swings move it. Capital spending of 3.18% of last-twelve-months sales and the cost savings the company cites from productivity and restructuring actions support conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow, 50.08% in fiscal 2025 and 45.84% over the last twelve months, while working capital absorbed USD 138.8 million in nine months of 2026 against USD 135.3 million a year earlier, a normal seasonal build. Cash interest, cash taxes and restructuring cash all sit below EBITDA, so the conversion is a better guide to debt service capacity than the EBITDA ratios.

### Ownership and financial policy

Avient is a public company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in the filings, and its consolidated perimeter is the only group structure supplied; borrower and guarantor perimeters and the priority of the notes against the secured term loan and revolver are not established. Financial policy shown by action is conservative: debt was prepaid from cash, no shares were repurchased, the dividend rose each year and no acquisition has been paid for since 2022, so leverage tolerance appears to have fallen as net leverage moved from 3.63x to 2.65x. The unexplained change of chief executive and chief financial officer in 2026, and a buyback authorisation that remains open, are the points that could change that policy.

### Industry forces and credit-translated SWOT

Competition is global and local: the company competes with global companies and local niche producers on performance, innovation, service, quality, delivery and price, and with polymer and non-polymer alternatives, so rivalry limits price increases beyond cost pass-through. Buyer power is dispersed because no customer exceeds 3% of revenue, while supplier power sits with large chemical producers, whose resin and additive prices Avient cannot control and, for some strategic materials, cannot easily replace. Trade policy and currency are the material external factors: the annual report names tariffs and retaliatory measures as risks to demand and results, 61% of sales are outside the United States, and the euro net investment is hedged with swaps whose liability is USD 302.0 million, so a stronger dollar or new tariffs would pressure translated earnings, while plastics and environmental regulation add compliance cost. In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, cash generation and diversification, the weaknesses are the maturity wall, legacy claims and swap-supported interest cost, the opportunities are growth in defense, healthcare, electronics and infrastructure applications where growth-vector sales are outpacing the rest of the company, and the threats are input-cost inflation without pricing, tariffs and a weaker refinancing market in 2029 to 2031.

### Outlook

Over the next 12 to 24 months the supports are pricing and mix, growth in defense, packaging and infrastructure demand, restructuring savings and lower interest from prepayments, while the pressures are input-cost inflation, tariffs, the Calvert City cost and timeline, tax claims and a fourth-quarter capital spending step-up toward the 2026 estimate of about USD 140 million. No guidance or forecast is supplied, so the outlook is qualitative: leverage should keep falling if the margin holds, but each of the pressures draws on cash that now goes to prepayment. Over three to five years the outlook is dominated by refinancing the term loan in 2029, the notes and revolver in 2030 and the 2031 notes, with swap maturities between 2027 and 2029 adding a possible cash call.

### Downside scenario

The realistic downside starts with raw-material, energy and freight costs rising faster than selling prices in packaging, consumer and industrial markets, which the annual report names as a risk. The first operational break is gross margin, because cost of sales is most of the cost base and pass-through has only been shown in an upswing. If EBITDA fell back to its fiscal 2025 reported level, a fall of USD 132.0 million, total debt would be 4.69x EBITDA and net debt 3.55x, and free cash flow after dividends would be about USD 6.6 million before tax relief and working-capital release, so debt reduction would stop and the prepayment would have to come from cash. Management levers are the dividend of USD 100.4 million a year, capital spending that runs at about 57% of depreciation and amortization, restructuring and the unused buyback authority, and liquidity of USD 932.4 million would absorb the shortfall, so liquidity distress before 2029 is not indicated. The consequence is on refinancing: the USD 470.7 million term loan due in 2029 becomes current in 2028 and would be refinanced at 3.55x to 4.69x leverage and with Calvert City costs still open. The observable triggers are a falling EBITDA margin, a lag between price and cost, a rising environmental accrual and a swap settlement.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Avient presents an adequate business profile supported by diversified customers, steady free cash flow and USD 932.4 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by a USD 1,847.6 million maturity wall from 2029 to 2031 and by legacy claims that are not bounded. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow of USD 239.0 million covers dividends of USD 100.4 million and low capital spending, although part of the 2026 earnings gain is charges leaving the window. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and 2029, the margin holding, the Calvert City accrual stabilising and the treatment of the swap liabilities. The primary downside path is a pricing squeeze that returns EBITDA toward its 2025 level and leaves less cushion for refinancing. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant levels, the swap schedule, interim cash interest, a peer set and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: refinancing of the 2029 to 2031 maturity wall.
